stewart_read: This is a classic 'not interested' style objection the schema flags for a flip (e.g., reframe around what they're not interested in). Rep instead asks 'why' and lets the customer lead into roof concerns.
alternative_hypothesis: Reactive: rep should have used the inversion flip here per script guidance.
coaching_implication: Practice the small-ask/curiosity flip on early hesitation instead of opening the door wide with 'why is that.'

quote: you know, I don't know what this is gonna do to my roof.
stewart_read: No canonical roof-damage rebuttal exists in the schema, but rep's response was thin reassurance without redirecting to specialist inspection value.
alternative_hypothesis: Strategic: rep may be trying to keep it simple and not scope-creep into engineering detail.
coaching_implication: A tighter response ties roof safety directly to the in-house inspection/report rather than a bare assurance.

quote: How long is the warranty? Because my roof has a lifetime warranty.
stewart_read: Rep answers a detailed warranty comparison question (panel years vs installation coverage) that is closer-tier content, rather than bridging to the specialist.
alternative_hypothesis: Reactive: rep engaged in technical warranty debate instead of the escape hatch line.
coaching_implication: Use the scope-discipline escape hatch: 'that's exactly what our specialist walks through in the design review' instead of quoting warranty terms.

quote: I I don't get a lot of sun. The more more I thought about it, I have the limited, amount of sun that gets on my roof.
stewart_read: Second self-generated objection in a row; rep's response about running a report and showing specific numbers is a good curiosity-creation move, distinct from the earlier scope-creep answer.
coaching_implication: This response is close to schema-correct — worth reinforcing as the template for shading pushback.

quote: it's no issues if it doesn't make sense for you. We just wanna see if we can can help you cut down on costs
stewart_read: Pressure-release line is the turning point of the call — customer re-engages immediately after.
coaching_implication: This no-obligation framing worked; keep it as a go-to when a customer stalls twice in a row.

quote: Well, right now, I'm driving, so I can't do it now.
stewart_read: Customer cannot capture the bill live; rep pivots to email capture but the bill is never actually sent during the call.
coaching_implication: Flag for follow-up — bill capture is unresolved and the appointment is conditioned on the customer sending it later.

quote: Can you just put that in an email or a text to me?
stewart_read: Call ends without the 'is that fair?' handshake, no-driving/computer instruction, or one-hour block statement — button-up was left incomplete per verified events.
coaching_implication: Even with a driving customer, rep should still verbally confirm the appointment terms (duration, what's needed) rather than relying entirely on a follow-up text.
